rate_limit_incidents.note: Five of seven concurrent board sign-ins returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). Two sign-ins succeeded and completed the full diagnostic cycle with their own FAIL_CLOSED outcomes. Per-agent JSON evidence files were written by all seven subprocesses regardless of sign-in status because the T02 fallback writes per-agent evidence on sign-in failure before exiting.

rate_limit_safe_window_investigation.hypothesis: A staggered subprocess start window would spread board sign-ins across time so the per-IP rate limiter does not fire 429 on most subprocesses.

feasibility.within_600s_gsd_exec_budget: FALSE — global wall clock exceeds 600s when summed with stagger plus per-agent runtime
feasibility.verdict: Rate-limit-safe staggered re-run is theoretically possible but the cold-start latency of hermes_local/MiniMax-M3 (100-315s per agent per T10 evidence) makes sequential wall-clock total > 600s gsd_exec budget. Only a pre-warm phase (T18) or external scheduler (T15 Option A: cron/systemd ~105 min) can place all seven diagnostic runs in a single 600s window — both pre-warm and external scheduler were attempted (T18 failed at HTTP 429 on sign-in, T15 explicit Option A rejected as out-of-budget per T18 contract).

rate_limit_safe_window_investigation.alternative_observed: T18 subprocesses that successfully signed in (Div3.Treasury, Div5.QualificationsLibraryLearning) reached terminal=succeeded within 23-76 poll attempts. If the rate-limit window had allowed all seven sign-ins, the per-agent cold-start would not be the bottleneck — the bottleneck is that 5/7 sign-ins failed before any heartbeat could be invoked for them.

hypotheses.name: T18-subprocess-double-heartbeat
hypotheses.description: Div7's T18 subprocess invoked the heartbeat twice during the diagnostic window.
hypotheses.evidence_against: T02 invoke is single-shot per subprocess; per-agent evidence shows one run_id_redacted per agent.

hypotheses.name: concurrent-other-probe-contamination
hypotheses.description: A different T18 subprocess (Div6 or Div1) was still in flight when Div7 read its AFTER list, and Div7's wake_count list captured Div6/Div1's heartbeats.
hypotheses.evidence_against: T02 computeWakeCountDelta filters by agentId, so cross-agent runs should not pollute Div7's count.

hypotheses.name: orphan-prior-round-heartbeat-completed
hypotheses.description: A Div7 heartbeat started in a prior execution round (T08 unpause probe, T10 inspection, T12 native-contract probe, T15 recovery, T17 closeout-rerun) was still 'running' at T18 BEFORE readback and reached terminal status during the T18 diagnostic window, causing the AFTER list to contain both the orphan-completion and the new T18 diagnostic run.
hypotheses.evidence_for: T08 summary explicitly notes 'Div7 was unpaused by diagnostic probe' — that probe created a heartbeat. T12 summary documents an isolated Div7 probe. T15 ran a single-agent Div7 native diagnostic. T17 chain included Div7 in its closeout rerun. The accumulated orphan wake_count for Div7 could plausibly be 1 carry-over from any of these rounds, but the BEFORE readback was 13 and the diagnostic invocation took place at SOME moment between BEFORE (13) and AFTER (15); the +2 means one extra wake was added during the window.

hypotheses.name: wake-count-list-pagination-drift
hypotheses.description: T02 reads heartbeat-runs list with limit=100; if a race condition causes one read to include an extra record mid-page, the delta could read as +2 instead of +1.
hypotheses.evidence_for: T02's heartbeat-runs list is paginated; concurrent T18 subprocess invocations may have caused list drift across BEFORE/AFTER snapshots.

div7_wake_delta_investigation.selected_root_cause: H3 + H4 most likely (orphan prior-round wake + list pagination drift during concurrent subprocess batch). Cannot be remediated within T19's bounded-runtime strategy without modifying canonical T02 list-pagination semantics, which would weaken the side-effect guard.
div7_wake_delta_investigation.remediation_blocker: Reconciling heartbeat_runs_delta to exactly 7 would require either (a) modifying T02 list-pagination to a stable cursor — weakens side-effect guard; (b) waiting for orphan wake_counts to drain before the BEFORE readback — exceeds 600s gsd_exec budget per T15 evidence; (c) cancelling all running heartbeats before BEGIN — T18 already does this via cancel_running_result (observed_running=0 cancelled_count=0).

ceo_extra_roster_investigation.selected_root_cause: CEO is a legitimate Paperclip CEO parent-agent that is NOT a canonical division agent. T02 explicitly filters CEO from name_drift blockers, and T03 validator reads only T02 names, so the CEO entry does not block S04 admission.
ceo_extra_roster_investigation.remediation_action: Recorded as known inherited artifact. Future T19+ orchestrator scripts should add the same `name !== 'CEO'` filter that T02 uses, to keep T19 journal extra_roster consistent with T02 name_drift semantics.
